17/// The 14 standard fonts of PDF.
18#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
19pub enum StandardFont {
20    /// Helvetica.
21    Helvetica,
22    /// Helvetica Bold.
23    HelveticaBold,
24    /// Helvetica Oblique.
25    HelveticaOblique,
26    /// Helvetica Bold Oblique.
27    HelveticaBoldOblique,
28    /// Courier.
29    Courier,
30    /// Courier Bold.
31    CourierBold,
32    /// Courier Oblique.
33    CourierOblique,
34    /// Courier Bold Oblique.
35    CourierBoldOblique,
36    /// Times Roman.
37    TimesRoman,
38    /// Times Bold.
39    TimesBold,
40    /// Times Italic.
41    TimesItalic,
42    /// Times Bold Italic.
43    TimesBoldItalic,
44    /// Zapf Dingbats - a decorative symbol font.
45    ZapfDingBats,
46    /// Symbol - a mathematical symbol font.
47    Symbol,
48}

50impl StandardFont {
51    pub(crate) fn code_to_name(&self, code: u8) -> Option<&'static str> {
52        match self {
53            Self::Symbol => symbol::get(code),
54            // Note that this font does not return postscript character names,
55            // but instead has a custom encoding.
56            Self::ZapfDingBats => zapf_dings::get(code),
57            _ => standard::get(code),
58        }
59    }
60
61    pub(crate) fn get_width(&self, mut name: &str) -> Option<f32> {
62        // <https://github.com/apache/pdfbox/blob/129aafe26548c1ff935af9c55cb40a996186c35f/pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/pdmodel/font/PDSimpleFont.java#L340>
63        if name == ".notdef" {
64            return Some(250.0);
65        }
66
67        name = normalized_glyph_name(name);
68
69        match self {
70            Self::Helvetica => metrics::HELVETICA.get(name).copied(),
71            Self::HelveticaBold => metrics::HELVETICA_BOLD.get(name).copied(),
72            Self::HelveticaOblique => metrics::HELVETICA_OBLIQUE.get(name).copied(),
73            Self::HelveticaBoldOblique => metrics::HELVETICA_BOLD_OBLIQUE.get(name).copied(),
74            Self::Courier => metrics::COURIER.get(name).copied(),
75            Self::CourierBold => metrics::COURIER_BOLD.get(name).copied(),
76            Self::CourierOblique => metrics::COURIER_OBLIQUE.get(name).copied(),
77            Self::CourierBoldOblique => metrics::COURIER_BOLD_OBLIQUE.get(name).copied(),
78            Self::TimesRoman => metrics::TIMES_ROMAN.get(name).copied(),
79            Self::TimesBold => metrics::TIMES_BOLD.get(name).copied(),
80            Self::TimesItalic => metrics::TIMES_ITALIC.get(name).copied(),
81            Self::TimesBoldItalic => metrics::TIMES_BOLD_ITALIC.get(name).copied(),
82            Self::ZapfDingBats => metrics::ZAPF_DING_BATS.get(name).copied(),
83            Self::Symbol => metrics::SYMBOL.get(name).copied(),
84        }
85    }

126    pub(crate) fn is_bold(&self) -> bool {
127        matches!(
128            self,
129            Self::HelveticaBold | Self::HelveticaBoldOblique | Self::CourierBold | Self::CourierBoldOblique | Self::TimesBold | Self::TimesBoldItalic
130        )
131    }
132
133    pub(crate) fn is_italic(&self) -> bool {
134        matches!(
135            self,
136            Self::HelveticaOblique
137                | Self::HelveticaBoldOblique
138                | Self::CourierOblique
139                | Self::CourierBoldOblique
140                | Self::TimesItalic
141                | Self::TimesBoldItalic
142        )
143    }
144
145    pub(crate) fn is_serif(&self) -> bool {
146        matches!(self, Self::TimesRoman | Self::TimesBold | Self::TimesItalic | Self::TimesBoldItalic)
147    }

149    pub(crate) fn is_monospace(&self) -> bool {
150        matches!(self, Self::Courier | Self::CourierBold | Self::CourierOblique | Self::CourierBoldOblique)
151    }

153    /// Return suitable font data for the given standard font.
154    ///
155    /// Currently, this will return the corresponding Foxit font, which is a set of permissibly
156    /// licensed fonts that is also very light-weight.
157    ///
158    /// You can use the result of this method in your implementation of [`FontResolverFn`].
159    ///
160    /// [`FontResolverFn`]: crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::FontResolverFn
161    pub fn get_font_data(&self) -> (FontData, u32) {
162        use std::sync::Arc;
163
164        let data = match self {
165            Self::Helvetica => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSans.pfb")[..],
166            Self::HelveticaBold => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSansBold.pfb")[..],
167            Self::HelveticaOblique => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSansItalic.pfb")[..],
168            Self::HelveticaBoldOblique => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSansBoldItalic.pfb")[..],
169            Self::Courier => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitFixed.pfb")[..],
170            Self::CourierBold => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitFixedBold.pfb")[..],
171            Self::CourierOblique => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitFixedItalic.pfb")[..],
172            Self::CourierBoldOblique => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitFixedBoldItalic.pfb")[..],
173            Self::TimesRoman => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSerif.pfb")[..],
174            Self::TimesBold => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSerifBold.pfb")[..],
175            Self::TimesItalic => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSerifItalic.pfb")[..],
176            Self::TimesBoldItalic => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSerifBoldItalic.pfb")[..],
177            Self::ZapfDingBats => &include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitDingbats.pfb")[..],
178            Self::Symbol => {
179                include_bytes!("../../../../assets/vendor/hayro-interpret/assets/FoxitSymbol.pfb")
180            }
181        };
182
183        (Arc::new(data), 0)
184    }
185}

187/// PdfCraft patch (98): the style names that may follow `Symbol` or `SymbolMT` after a `,` or
188/// `-` and still name the Symbol font (any case).
189const SYMBOL_STYLES: [&str; 9] = ["Bold", "Italic", "BoldItalic", "Oblique", "BoldOblique", "Regular", "Roman", "Normal", "Plain"];
190
191/// PdfCraft patch (98): whether `name` (without a subset prefix) is `Symbol` or `SymbolMT`, alone
192/// or followed by `,` or `-` and a style from [`SYMBOL_STYLES`]. Another name after the
193/// separator (`Symbol-Helvetica`) is a different font.
194fn is_symbol_name(name: &str) -> bool {
195    let (family, style) = match name.split_once([',', '-']) {
196        Some((family, style)) => (family, Some(style)),
197        None => (name, None),
198    };
199    matches!(family, "Symbol" | "SymbolMT") && style.is_none_or(|style| SYMBOL_STYLES.iter().any(|s| s.eq_ignore_ascii_case(style)))
200}
201
202enum StandardFontFamily {
203    Helvetica,
204    Courier,
205    Times,
206}
207
208pub(crate) fn select_standard_font(dict: &Dict<'_>, descriptor: &Dict<'_>) -> Option<(StandardFont, bool)> {
209    let base_font = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(BASE_FONT)?;
210    let name = strip_subset_prefix(base_font.as_str());
211
212    // First try whether it matches literally.
213    match name {
214        "Helvetica" => return Some((StandardFont::Helvetica, true)),
215        "Helvetica-Bold" => return Some((StandardFont::HelveticaBold, true)),
216        "Helvetica-Oblique" => return Some((StandardFont::HelveticaOblique, true)),
217        "Helvetica-BoldOblique" => return Some((StandardFont::HelveticaBoldOblique, true)),
218        "Courier" => return Some((StandardFont::Courier, true)),
219        "Courier-Bold" => return Some((StandardFont::CourierBold, true)),
220        "Courier-Oblique" => return Some((StandardFont::CourierOblique, true)),
221        "Courier-BoldOblique" => return Some((StandardFont::CourierBoldOblique, true)),
222        "Times-Roman" => return Some((StandardFont::TimesRoman, true)),
223        "Times-Bold" => return Some((StandardFont::TimesBold, true)),
224        "Times-Italic" => return Some((StandardFont::TimesItalic, true)),
225        "Times-BoldItalic" => return Some((StandardFont::TimesBoldItalic, true)),
226        "Symbol" => return Some((StandardFont::Symbol, true)),
227        "ZapfDingbats" => return Some((StandardFont::ZapfDingBats, true)),
228        _ => {}
229    }
230
231    // PdfCraft patch (98): `SymbolMT` (the name Symbol has as a TrueType font) and the style
232    // variants `Symbol,Bold`, `SymbolMT,Italic` or `Symbol-Bold` are the Symbol font, drawn with
233    // its built-in encoding like `Symbol` itself, whatever `/Encoding` and flags they declare.
234    if is_symbol_name(name) {
235        return Some((StandardFont::Symbol, true));
236    }
237
238    // Now, we bruteforce, trying to determine a suitable font based on the
239    // keywords that appear in the name.
240    let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
241
242    let is_bold = descriptor.get::<u32>(FONT_WEIGHT).is_some_and(|w| w >= 700) || lower.contains("bold") || lower.contains("demi");
243    let is_italic = descriptor.get::<f32>(ITALIC_ANGLE).is_some_and(|a| a != 0.0) || lower.contains("italic") || lower.contains("oblique");
244
245    let (family, exact) = if lower.contains("helvetica") {
246        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Helvetica), true)
247    } else if lower.contains("arial") || lower.contains("sans") {
248        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Helvetica), false)
249    } else if lower.contains("courier") {
250        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Courier), true)
251    } else if lower.contains("mono") {
252        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Courier), false)
253    } else if lower.contains("times") {
254        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Times), true)
255    } else if lower.contains("serif") {
256        (Some(StandardFontFamily::Times), false)
257    } else if lower.contains("zapfdingbats") || lower.contains("dingbats") {
258        return Some((StandardFont::ZapfDingBats, false));
259    } else {
260        (None, false)
261    };
262
263    let font = match (family?, is_bold, is_italic) {
264        (StandardFontFamily::Helvetica, false, false) => StandardFont::Helvetica,
265        (StandardFontFamily::Helvetica, true, false) => StandardFont::HelveticaBold,
266        (StandardFontFamily::Helvetica, false, true) => StandardFont::HelveticaOblique,
267        (StandardFontFamily::Helvetica, true, true) => StandardFont::HelveticaBoldOblique,
268        (StandardFontFamily::Courier, false, false) => StandardFont::Courier,
269        (StandardFontFamily::Courier, true, false) => StandardFont::CourierBold,
270        (StandardFontFamily::Courier, false, true) => StandardFont::CourierOblique,
271        (StandardFontFamily::Courier, true, true) => StandardFont::CourierBoldOblique,
272        (StandardFontFamily::Times, false, false) => StandardFont::TimesRoman,
273        (StandardFontFamily::Times, true, false) => StandardFont::TimesBold,
274        (StandardFontFamily::Times, false, true) => StandardFont::TimesItalic,
275        (StandardFontFamily::Times, true, true) => StandardFont::TimesBoldItalic,
276    };
277
278    Some((font, exact))
279}

281#[derive(Debug)]
282pub(crate) enum StandardFontBlob {
283    Cff(CffFontBlob),
284    Otf(OpenTypeFontBlob, HashMap<String, GlyphId>),
285}
286
287impl StandardFontBlob {
288    pub(crate) fn from_data(data: FontData, index: u32) -> Option<Self> {
289        if let Some(blob) = CffFontBlob::new(data.clone()) {
290            Some(Self::new_cff(blob))
291        } else {
292            OpenTypeFontBlob::new(data, index).map(Self::new_otf)
293        }
294    }
295
296    pub(crate) fn new_cff(blob: CffFontBlob) -> Self {
297        Self::Cff(blob)
298    }
299
300    pub(crate) fn new_otf(blob: OpenTypeFontBlob) -> Self {
301        let glyph_names = blob.glyph_names();
302        Self::Otf(blob, glyph_names)
303    }
304}
305
306impl StandardFontBlob {
307    pub(crate) fn name_to_glyph(&self, name: &str) -> Option<GlyphId> {
308        match self {
309            Self::Cff(blob) => blob.glyph_index_by_name(name),
310            Self::Otf(_, glyph_names) => glyph_names.get(name).copied(),
311        }
312    }
313
314    pub(crate) fn unicode_to_glyph(&self, code: u32) -> Option<GlyphId> {
315        match self {
316            Self::Cff(_) => None,
317            Self::Otf(blob, _) => blob.font_ref().cmap().ok().and_then(|c| c.map_codepoint(code)),
318        }
319    }
320
321    pub(crate) fn advance_width(&self, glyph: GlyphId) -> Option<f32> {
322        match self {
323            // PdfCraft patch (77): the stand-in's own advance, so a glyph drawn wider than the
324            // standard metrics (the € of the bundled stand-ins) is fitted to them.
325            Self::Cff(blob) => blob.advance_width(glyph),
326            Self::Otf(blob, _) => blob.glyph_metrics().advance_width(glyph),
327        }
328    }
329
330    pub(crate) fn outline_glyph(&self, glyph: GlyphId) -> BezPath {
331        // Standard fonts have empty outlines for these, but in Liberation Sans
332        // they are a .notdef rectangle.
333        if glyph == GlyphId::NOTDEF {
334            return BezPath::new();
335        }
336
337        match self {
338            Self::Cff(blob) => blob.outline_glyph(glyph),
339            Self::Otf(blob, _) => blob.outline_glyph(glyph),
340        }
341    }
342}

344#[derive(Debug)]
345pub(crate) struct StandardKind {
346    base_font: StandardFont,
347    base_font_blob: StandardFontBlob,
348    encoding: Encoding,
349    widths: Vec<Width>,
350    missing_width: f32,
351    fallback: bool,
352    glyph_to_code: RefCell<HashMap<GlyphId, u8>>,
353    encodings: HashMap<u8, String>,
354}
355
356impl StandardKind {
357    pub(crate) fn new(dict: &Dict<'_>, resolver: &FontResolverFn) -> Option<Self> {
358        let descriptor = dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(FONT_DESC).unwrap_or_default();
359        let (font, exact) = select_standard_font(dict, &descriptor)?;
360        Self::new_with_standard(dict, font, !exact, resolver)
361    }
362
363    pub(crate) fn new_with_standard(dict: &Dict<'_>, base_font: StandardFont, fallback: bool, resolver: &FontResolverFn) -> Option<Self> {
364        let descriptor = dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(FONT_DESC).unwrap_or_default();
365        let (widths, missing_width) = read_widths(dict, &descriptor)?;
366
367        let (mut encoding, encoding_map) = read_encoding(dict);
368
369        // See PDFJS-16464: Ignore encodings for non-embedded Type1 symbol fonts.
370        if matches!(base_font, StandardFont::Symbol | StandardFont::ZapfDingBats) {
371            encoding = Encoding::BuiltIn;
372        }
373
374        let (blob, index) = resolver(&FontQuery::Standard(base_font))?;
375        let base_font_blob = StandardFontBlob::from_data(blob, index)?;
376
377        Some(Self {
378            base_font,
379            base_font_blob,
380            widths,
381            missing_width,
382            encodings: encoding_map,
383            glyph_to_code: RefCell::new(HashMap::new()),
384            fallback,
385            encoding,
386        })
387    }
388
389    pub(crate) fn code_to_ps_name(&self, code: u8) -> Option<&str> {
390        let bf = self.base_font;
391
392        self.encodings.get(&code).map(String::as_str).or_else(|| match self.encoding {
393            Encoding::BuiltIn => bf.code_to_name(code),
394            _ => self.encoding.map_code(code),
395        })
396    }
397
398    pub(crate) fn map_code(&self, code: u8) -> GlyphId {
399        let result = self
400            .code_to_ps_name(code)
401            .and_then(|c| {
402                self.base_font_blob
403                    .name_to_glyph(c)
404                    .or_else(|| {
405                        // If the font doesn't have a POST table, try to map via unicode instead.
406                        glyph_names::get(c).and_then(|c| self.base_font_blob.unicode_to_glyph(c.chars().nth(0).unwrap() as u32))
407                    })
408                    // PdfCraft patch: an accented letter the stand-in lacks is built from its
409                    // parts (see `ACCENTED_LETTERS`).
410                    .or_else(|| self.composite_glyph(code, c))
411            })
412            .unwrap_or(GlyphId::NOTDEF);
413        self.glyph_to_code.borrow_mut().insert(result, code);
414
415        result
416    }
417
418    /// PdfCraft patch: the glyph id standing for the letter `name` built from its base letter and
419    /// accent, when the stand-in has both. Ids from [`COMPOSITE_GLYPH_BASE`] up are one per
420    /// character code, so the outline is found again from the code alone.
421    fn composite_glyph(&self, code: u8, name: &str) -> Option<GlyphId> {
422        let (base, accent, _) = accented_parts(name)?;
423        self.base_font_blob.name_to_glyph(base)?;
424        self.base_font_blob.name_to_glyph(accent)?;
425        Some(GlyphId::new(COMPOSITE_GLYPH_BASE + u32::from(code)))
426    }
427
428    /// PdfCraft patch: the outline of a glyph from [`Self::composite_glyph`] — the base letter,
429    /// then the accent centred on it. An accent above a letter taller than `x` is raised by the
430    /// difference (the stand-in's accents sit on lowercase letters) and, in an italic font,
431    /// moved along the slant; an ogonek hangs from the letter's right edge; a comma below is
432    /// the font's comma, smaller, under the baseline.
433    fn composite_outline(&self, glyph: GlyphId) -> Option<BezPath> {
434        let code = u8::try_from(glyph.to_u32().checked_sub(COMPOSITE_GLYPH_BASE)?).ok()?;
435        let (base, accent, place) = accented_parts(self.code_to_ps_name(code)?)?;
436        let outline = |name: &str| self.base_font_blob.name_to_glyph(name).map(|g| self.base_font_blob.outline_glyph(g));
437        let mut path = outline(base)?;
438        let mut accent = outline(accent)?;
439        if path.elements().is_empty() || accent.elements().is_empty() {
440            return Some(path);
441        }
442        if place == Place::CommaBelow {
443            accent = Affine::scale(COMMA_BELOW_SCALE) * accent;
444        }
445        let (b, a) = (path.bounding_box(), accent.bounding_box());
446        let (dx, dy) = match place {
447            Place::Below => (b.center().x - a.center().x, 0.0),
448            Place::CommaBelow => {
449                // Its top a little below the baseline (or the letter's overshoot below it), and
450                // in an italic font moved back along the slant by as much as it is lowered.
451                let dy = b.y0.min(0.0) - COMMA_BELOW_GAP * a.height() - a.y1;
452                let slant = if self.base_font.is_italic() { dy * ITALIC_ACCENT_SLANT } else { 0.0 };
453                (b.center().x - a.center().x + slant, dy)
454            }
455            Place::Ogonek => (b.x1 - a.x1, 0.0),
456            Place::Above => {
457                let x_top = outline("x").filter(|x| !x.elements().is_empty()).map_or(b.y1, |x| x.bounding_box().y1);
458                // Overshoot of round lowercase letters (o, g, s) over x is not a taller letter.
459                let raise = if b.y1 > x_top * 1.1 { b.y1 - x_top } else { 0.0 };
460                let slant = if self.base_font.is_italic() { raise * ITALIC_ACCENT_SLANT } else { 0.0 };
461                (b.center().x - a.center().x + slant, raise)
462            }
463        };
464        if !(dx.is_finite() && dy.is_finite()) {
465            return Some(path);
466        }
467        path.extend(Affine::translate((dx, dy)) * accent);
468        Some(path)
469    }
470
471    pub(crate) fn outline_glyph(&self, glyph: GlyphId) -> BezPath {
472        let composite = self.composite_outline(glyph);
473        let is_composite = composite.is_some();
474        let path = composite.unwrap_or_else(|| self.base_font_blob.outline_glyph(glyph));
475
476        // If the font is not embedded, we might need to stretch it so that
477        // it matches the metrics of the actual underlying font blob.
478
479        // PdfCraft patch: a composite id isn't a glyph of the blob, so its width comes from the
480        // standard metrics of its name.
481        let blob_width = if is_composite { None } else { self.base_font_blob.advance_width(glyph) };
482        if let Some(code) = self.glyph_to_code.borrow().get(&glyph).copied()
483            && let Some(actual_width) = blob_width.or_else(|| self.code_to_ps_name(code).and_then(|name| self.base_font.get_width(name)))
484        {
485            // From my experiments: Most PDF viewers, if they detect a font is a
486            // standard font, they completely ignore the widths array, even if
487            // different widths are indicated there. So only if it's an unknown
488            // font do we check the widths array. Otherwise, we always use the
489            // base font metrics.
490            let should_width = if self.fallback {
491                if let Some(Width::Value(w)) = self.widths.get(code as usize).copied() {
492                    w
493                } else {
494                    return path;
495                }
496            } else if let Some(w) = self.code_to_ps_name(code).and_then(|name| self.base_font.get_width(name)) {
497                w
498            } else {
499                return path;
500            };
501
502            // PdfCraft patch (57): a stand-in for a font the document names is narrowed to a
503            // narrower /Widths advance, so neighbours don't overlap, but never widened: the
504            // advance already places the next glyph, and widening drew `i` and `l` of a 600-unit
505            // `Arial,Bold` as solid blocks twice their width.
506            let should_width = if self.fallback { should_width.min(actual_width) } else { should_width };
507            return stretch_glyph(path, should_width, actual_width);
508        }
509
510        path
511    }
512
513    pub(crate) fn glyph_width(&self, code: u8) -> Option<f32> {
514        match self.widths.get(code as usize).copied() {
515            Some(Width::Value(w)) => Some(w),
516            Some(Width::Missing) => Some(self.missing_width),
517            None => self.code_to_ps_name(code).and_then(|c| self.base_font.get_width(c)),
518        }
519    }
520
521    pub(crate) fn char_code_to_unicode(&self, code: u8) -> Option<char> {
522        // PdfCraft patch: an Annex D.2 alias code reads as the ordinary character; see
523        // `Encoding::text_alias`. `code_to_ps_name` is shared with glyph lookup and stays as it
524        // is, so the alias is applied here, after `/Differences` has had its say.
525        if !self.encodings.contains_key(&code)
526            && let Some(name) = self.encoding.text_alias(code)
527        {
528            return glyph_name_to_unicode(name);
529        }
530        self.code_to_ps_name(code).and_then(glyph_name_to_unicode)
531    }
532
533    pub(crate) fn is_italic(&self) -> bool {
534        self.base_font.is_italic()
535    }
536
537    pub(crate) fn is_bold(&self) -> bool {
538        self.base_font.is_bold()
539    }
540
541    pub(crate) fn is_serif(&self) -> bool {
542        self.base_font.is_serif()
543    }
544
545    pub(crate) fn is_monospace(&self) -> bool {
546        self.base_font.is_monospace()
547    }
548}

575/// PdfCraft patch: the stand-ins for the standard fonts (PDFium's Foxit fonts) carry only the
576/// glyphs of the Standard, WinAnsi and Mac Roman encodings, so a font that isn't embedded and
577/// names other Latin letters in its /Differences (`/Gbreve`, `/Idotaccent`, `/Scedilla`…, as
578/// iText 2 writes Turkish text with Times New Roman left unembedded) drew nothing for them. Each of
579/// these Latin Extended-A letters is a base letter the stand-ins have plus one of their accents,
580/// as Type 1 `seac` composites and the composites of the standard-14 AFM files are built.

690/// PdfCraft patch: the comma-below letters of [`ACCENTED_LETTERS`] by character. The glyph list
691/// names the Latvian ones `Kcedilla`… (their comma is a cedilla in Unicode's names), has no name
692/// for Ț ț, and gives `Tcommaaccent` and `tcommaaccent` to Ţ ţ, which keep their cedilla.
693const COMMA_BELOW_BY_CHAR: &[(char, &str)] = &[
694    ('\u{0122}', "Gcommaaccent"),
695    ('\u{0136}', "Kcommaaccent"),
696    ('\u{0137}', "kcommaaccent"),
697    ('\u{013B}', "Lcommaaccent"),
698    ('\u{013C}', "lcommaaccent"),
699    ('\u{0145}', "Ncommaaccent"),
700    ('\u{0146}', "ncommaaccent"),
701    ('\u{0156}', "Rcommaaccent"),
702    ('\u{0157}', "rcommaaccent"),
703    ('\u{0218}', "Scommaaccent"),
704    ('\u{0219}', "scommaaccent"),
705    ('\u{021A}', "Tcommaaccent"),
706    ('\u{021B}', "tcommaaccent"),
707];

709/// PdfCraft patch: the base letter, accent and placement of an accented letter in
710/// [`ACCENTED_LETTERS`], by glyph name (`uni011E` and `u011E` forms too). A comma-below letter
711/// is found by its character ([`COMMA_BELOW_BY_CHAR`]), so `/uni0136` and `/Kcedilla` are Ķ too.
712fn accented_parts(name: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str, Place)> {
713    let name = normalized_glyph_name(name);
714    let by_name = |n: &str| ACCENTED_LETTERS.iter().find(|(letter, ..)| *letter == n).map(|&(_, base, accent, place)| (base, accent, place));
715    by_name(name).or_else(|| {
716        // Drawing keeps upstream's lenient reading of `uni` names; text goes by the glyph list
717        // specification (PdfCraft patch 92).
718        let c = glyph_names::get(name).and_then(|s| s.chars().next()).or_else(|| unicode_from_name(name))?;
719        match COMMA_BELOW_BY_CHAR.iter().find(|(letter, _)| *letter == c) {
720            Some((_, comma_below)) => by_name(comma_below),
721            None => by_name(glyph_names::get_reverse(c)?),
722        }
723    })
724}
